title: Modeling The Object Representations Underlying Human Physical Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2602.12486v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Humans appear to represent objects when reasoning about physics with coarse, volumetric "bodies" that smooth concavities, trading fine visual detail for efficient physical predictions. Yet, the structure of these representations remains largely unknown. Segmentation models, in contrast, are trained for pixel-accurate masks that may misalign with such bodies. We ask whether and when these models nonetheless acquire human-like object representations. Using a time-to-collision (TTC) and change detection (CD) behavioral task with data from 178 and 50 human participants, respectively, we introduce a pipeline and an alignment metric to compare the visual representations of segmentation models to those of humans. We do this systematically on multiple architectures (DINOv2, SegFormer, DeepLabV3+, and UPerNet), varying their size and training time. translated_title: 建模人类物理推理背后的物体表征
translated_abstract: 人类在推理物理问题时，似乎以粗糙的、体积化的“躯体”来表征物体，这种表征会平滑掉凹陷部分，以牺牲精细视觉细节为代价换取高效的物理预测。然而，这些表征的结构在很大程度上仍是未知的。相比之下，分割模型被训练用于生成像素级精确的掩码，这可能与这类“躯体”并不吻合。我们探究这些模型是否以及在何种情况下仍会获得类人的物体表征。利用碰撞时间（TTC）和变化检测（CD）两种行为任务，分别收集了178名和50名人类参与者的数据，我们提出了一个分析流程和一个对齐度量，用于比较分割模型与人类的视觉表征。我们在多种架构（DINOv2、SegFormer、DeepLabV3+和UPerNet）上系统地开展了实验，并改变模型的规模与训练时长。我们发现训练时间较短的模型分割物体过于粗糙，与人类的对齐较差……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过碰撞时间与变化检测行为任务及新提出的对齐度量，系统比较了多种分割模型与人类的物体表征，揭示了模型规模和训练时长如何影响其物体表征与人类物理推理所用表征的相似程度。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares object representations of segmentation models with those of humans using TTC and change detection behavioral tasks and a novel alignment metric, revealing how model size and training duration shape the human-likeness of these representations.
